extracted.intended_audience: ORR stakeholders: legal representatives, care provider facilities, sponsors, child welfare advocates, agency staff, and other commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed ORR regulations governing risk determination hearings for unaccompanied children, establishment and operation of a UC Office of the Ombuds, related procedures (appeals, confidentiality, access), and the regulatory/cost analyses to accompany the rulemaking. Intended to solicit public comment and set binding administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and purpose of risk determination hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental question at issue in an ORR risk determination hearing is whether an unaccompanied child would pose a danger to the community if released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk determination hearings are not bond hearings tied to payment; they determine danger to the community. ORR does not consider runaway risk when making release decisions; therefore risk determination hearings focus on dangerousness only. For the great majority, ORR has determined they are not a danger and placed in non-restrictive placements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must/ may receive a risk determination hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: All unaccompanied children in restrictive placements would be afforded a risk determination hearing before an independent HHS hearing officer, unless the child indicates in writing they refuse such a hearing; other children in ORR custody may request such a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing by the child, their attorney of record, or parent/legal guardian using an ORR form or other written request containing the same information. Children in restrictive placements based on a finding of dangerousness would automatically be provided a hearing unless they decline in writing; they may decline at any time, including after consultation with counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and process for requesting hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests under this section must be made in writing by specified parties using an ORR-provided form or a separate written request containing the information requested in ORR's form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to establish a process for providing notifications and receiving requests related to risk determination hearings; the child, attorney of record, or parent/legal guardian may submit requests to the care provider facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR initial burden of production
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would bear an initial burden of production, providing relevant arguments and documents to support its determination that an unaccompanied child would pose a danger if discharged from ORR care and custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initial production is intended to supply the factual and documentary basis for ORR's determination so the hearing officer and child have access to the documents and arguments relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unaccompanied child's burden of persuasion and standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The unaccompanied child would have the burden of persuasion to show that they would not be a danger to the community if released, under a preponderance of the evidence standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR notes it has a subregulatory process to ensure timely access to case files and documents for children and their legal counsel for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of the child at hearing (representation and evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unaccompanied child would be able to be represented by a person of the child's choosing, permitted to present oral and written evidence to the hearing officer, and to appear by video or teleconference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR is proposing these procedures to ensure the roles of each party are clear; ORR may also present evidence in writing or by appearing in person or via video/teleconference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding effect of hearing officer non-dangerousness decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision that an unaccompanied child would not be a danger to the community if released would be binding upon ORR unless appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR believes such decisions must be available for appeal if the child is found dangerous; however, the hearing officer's finding that a child is not dangerous must be honored by ORR unless an appeal overturns it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals channel and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions under this section may be appealed to the Assistant Secretary of ACF, or the Assistant Secretary's designee; appeal requests must be in writing and received within 30 days of the hearing officer's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an administrative appellate route within HHS to provide protections analogous to DOJ's Board of Immigration Appeals given HHS's lack of a two-tier appellate system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals standard of review (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary, or their designee, will reverse a hearing officer decision only if there is a clear error of fact, or if the decision includes an error of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR is proposing this constrained reversal standard but is also seeking comment on an alternative de novo review approach where the official would re-decide the issues without being constrained to clear error or law-only reversals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay of release on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the Assistant Secretary would not effect a stay of a hearing officer's decision finding non-dangerousness and resulting in release, unless the Assistant Secretary or their designee issues a written decision within five business days that release would likely result in a danger to the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any stay decision must include a description of behaviors while in ORR custody and/or documented criminal or juvenile behavior records showing the child would present a danger if released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and re‑hearing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions under this section would be final and binding on the Department for release considerations; a child determined to pose a danger may seek another hearing only by demonstrating a material change in circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may request a hearing officer make a new determination if at least one month has passed since the original decision and/or ORR can show a material change in circumstances. ORR believes one month is a reasonable interval to balance operational constraints with safety concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: hearings cannot order release or determine sponsor suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: This section cannot be used to determine whether an unaccompanied child has a suitable sponsor, and neither the hearing officer nor the Assistant Secretary would be authorized to order the child released or change placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release and placement decision-making authority remains vested in the Director of ORR under the HSA and TVPRA; the hearing's purpose is solely to determine danger to the community if released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: hearings not for placement or custody level decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk determination hearings may not be invoked to determine an unaccompanied child's placement while in ORR custody or to determine level of custody for the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR would determine placement and level of custody as part of ordinary placement procedures, though it may take into consideration the hearing officer's decision on level of danger for those purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of UC Office of the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose establishment of an independent UC Office of the Ombuds to receive, investigate, and informally address complaints about government actions affecting unaccompanied children, make findings and recommendations, and publish reports when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ombuds would be independent, impartial, and confidential, serve as a neutral third party (not a legal advocate), and would not have authority to compel ORR but could refer concerns to other federal agencies or entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core standards for the Ombuds office
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence, confidentiality, and impartiality are core standards; ombuds offices are informal, do not make binding decisions, and commit to credible practices, fairness, and assistance in resolution without providing formal rights-based remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR reviewed national ombuds literature (ACUS, ABA, IOA, USOA, COFO) and intends the UC Office of the Ombuds to incorporate those lessons and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting structure and organizational independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Ombuds will report directly to the ACF Assistant Secretary and be managed as a distinct entity separate from the UC Program to preserve independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR requests input on options relating to placement and reporting structure within ORR or elsewhere in ACF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policies, standards, and procedures for the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Office of the Ombuds shall develop and make publicly available the office's standards, practices, policies and procedures, giving consideration to nationally recognized ombuds organizations' recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR requests comments on which organizations' standards (ABA, IOA, USOA, COFO, etc.) the office should adopt and seeks input identifying potential standards and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outreach, accessibility, and notice requirements for the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ombuds must ensure contact information and scope/responsibilities are publicly available and provide notice to unaccompanied children, sponsors, and others in English and other languages spoken by the children, in an accessible manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should include auxiliary aids and services, clear and easily understood language, concise/ concrete sentences and/or visual aids. ORR expects multiple outreach approaches (flyers, facility postings, website, onsite visits) and would allow the Ombuds discretion to determine best outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Ombuds activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Office of the Ombuds' scope may include reviewing ORR compliance with Federal law, visiting facilities, investigating access-to-service issues, reviewing policy implementation, reviewing individual circumstances (access to services, transfers, discharge), and providing education about ORR and relevant legal/regulatory landscapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Ombuds may request information and documents from ORR and care provider facilities and shall be provided with them to the fullest extent possible. The Ombuds may recommend policy/process improvements and publish aggregated information annually about concerns received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral authority of Ombuds (non‑enforcement role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Ombuds is not an enforcement entity, it should have discretion to refer matters to other offices/entities (e.g., state/local law enforcement, OIG) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR frames the Ombuds as a neutral investigator and conciliator, with referral power but not enforcement authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and investigatory powers for Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ombuds must be able to meet with unaccompanied children upon receiving a complaint or based on findings, have access to ORR facilities, premises, and case file information, and have access to care provider and Federal staff responsible for the children's care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These powers are proposed to enable meaningful investigation and resolution of individual and systemic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational qualifications and staffing for Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Ombuds should be hired as a career civil servant with sufficient professional stature and requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities (e.g., informal dispute resolution, process design, training, data analysis, facilitation), and may engage additional staff as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes minimum qualifications including membership in relevant organizations or state bar, expertise in dispute resolution, child welfare, oversight/regulatory matters, and knowledge of ORR policy/regulations. The Ombuds shall establish procedures for training, certification, and continuing education for staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality requirements for Ombuds communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Records and proceedings should be kept confidential except to address an imminent risk of serious harm or in response to judicial action; the Ombuds is prohibited from using or sharing information for immigration enforcement purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality is paramount to encourage reporting; ORR requests comments on best practices for preserving confidentiality and building trust, and proposes that the Ombuds may accept anonymous reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of anonymous reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The UC Office of the Ombuds may accept reports from anonymous reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is proposed to encourage reporting of concerns while maintaining confidentiality and safety for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection and PRA considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, agencies must provide 60-day notice and solicit public comment before submitting an information collection to OMB; this proposed rule does not require information collections for which HHS plans to seek OMB approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals or other requests that require submission of information subsequent to an administrative action are not subject to the PRA under 5 CFR 1320.4(a)(2). ORR reviewed existing OMB control numbers and determined most reporting/recordkeeping burdens are already covered; ORR is not proposing new requirements that change burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation resource and cost assumptions for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR estimates it will require approximately 2,000-4,000 hours (six to 12 staff working full-time for two months) to implement the shift of responsibility for these hearings from DOJ to HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR expects initial resource requirements to fall on DOJ and HHS staff to create the new system; after implementation, ORR estimates no change in net resources required for hearings and seeks public comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed staffing and cost estimate for Office of the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR anticipates the Ombuds would be a GS-15 and support staff would include one GS-14, four GS-13s, and four GS-12s (assumed Step 5) and includes an overhead factor of 36.25%; total estimated annual cost approximately $1,718,529.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR derived the estimate by conferring with budgetary experts and analyzing likely caseload needs; ORR welcomes comments on staffing and structure. ORR also notes costs of maintaining compliance are allowable grant costs under 45 CFR 75.403–.405 and supplemental funding requests may be allowed for grantees that cannot absorb unbudgeted costs.
